messages:
anna: Quick check — we have a customer report where a route is getting the feature even though org=false, project=true, model=true, route=false. What's our precedence for flags?

mike: short answer: most-specific wins. precedence we landed on: route > model > project > org. so route=false should block.

sophia: to add context: model flags are useful for turning on model-specific behavior across many routes, but route-level configs must be able to override for traffic shaping/canaries. that was the design decision.

anna: ok that matches intuition. can someone post a quick example of how this looks in our flag config and how to check effective value?

mike: example (pseudo-yaml):

```
flags:
  enable_new_token_cache:
    org: false
    project: true
    model: true        # rw-turbo-v2
    route: false       # /v1/chat/assistant
```

Effective: false (route wins).

To check in CLI: `rw flags resolve --flag enable_new_token_cache --route /v1/chat/assistant --model rw-turbo-v2 --project search-team` -> prints effective value + list of sources.

sophia: also note: partial canaries are supported at route level only (percent or segment). if a route defines a canary, it replaces project/model canaries instead of merging.

anna: good call. so precedence for canary audiences is same: route canary > model canary > project canary > org default.

lia: guardrail reminder: any route-level canary >20% requires a quick security/monitoring sign-off in #incidents before rollout. we should codify that in the runbook.

mike: agreed. also suggest we expose an API `GET /flags/effective?route=...&model=...` for UI and infra checks (returns stack like org: false, project: true, model: true, route: false).

sophia: implemented stub in the config service PR #3127 — it returns a list of sources and final value. mike — can you add to the CLI to surface the stack?

mike: yea I'll add it. targetting a small patch today.

anna: action items: mike -> CLI change to show stack + `rw flags resolve` output. sophia -> add guardrail text to runbook about >20% canary sign-off. lia -> draft short incident-check checklist. I'll follow up to update product docs about precedence.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary rollout started for /v1/chat/assistant (flag: enable_stream_compaction) -> 5% internal seg.

anna: thanks — if anyone sees weird behavior in telemetry after the CLI change, ping me here and paste the `rw flags resolve` output. :thumbsup:
